Traffic-control devices include signals, signs, road markings and directions from police, highway workers or school crossing guards. A right turn on red is the stated exception to waiting for green, but only after the required stop and when no sign prohibits the turn. At a flashing yellow light, reduce speed and proceed carefully while preparing to stop for entering traffic. A flashing red signal requires a full stop behind the line, crosswalk or intersection, followed by yielding before proceeding. A green arrow permits a turn in its indicated direction after yielding to vehicles and pedestrians. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. narration.text: Red sign coloring identifies a prohibition or stop requirement, while green commonly supplies directions or guidance. Brown provides recreational or tourist guidance, pink identifies incident management and purple denotes EZPass information. An eight-sided sign means stop, while a downward-pointing triangular sign means yield. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Rectangular signs provide regulations or directions, and a five-sided sign identifies a school zone or school crossing. A circular sign warns in advance about a railroad crossing, while the crossbuck marks the crossing's location. A stop sign requires the wheels to become stationary behind the stop line or crosswalk, or before entering the intersection if neither exists. A circular railroad warning with black railroad letters signals the need to slow or stop and look and listen for rail traffic before crossing. When rail traffic approaches, stop behind the stop line or between fifteen and fifty feet from the nearest rail. At a crossing with multiple tracks, do not cross until you can see clearly along the tracks in both directions. Once a railroad crossing is clear, look in both directions and traverse the tracks promptly without stopping on them. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. narration.text: Work-zone signs usually have black lettering or symbols on orange diamond or rectangular backgrounds. Work-zone warnings can identify workers, lower speeds, detours, slow construction vehicles or sudden surface changes. Obey a work-zone flagger's directions about movement, speed and stopping. Cones, drums, panels and other barriers guide traffic and prevent entry into hazardous or closed areas. A work zone can use temporary signals; reduce speed, anticipate an abrupt stop and avoid close following. When work-zone fines are doubled, the increase is indicated before the driver enters the zone. Road markings separate lanes, show passing or lane-change permissions, assign turning lanes and identify pedestrian or stopping areas. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

lines.text: Broken white lines divide traffic moving in the same direction, while broken yellow lines divide
opposing flows.

narration.text: Broken white lines divide traffic moving in the same direction, while broken yellow lines divide opposing flows. Crossing a broken lane line to pass is permitted only when the maneuver is safe. The manual prohibits passing or changing lanes across a solid white line. Where parallel lines differ, the line nearest your vehicle controls passing: a solid line prohibits it, while a broken line permits a safe pass. Road-edge lines are white on two-way roads and at a one-way road's right edge, with yellow at its left edge. Stop at the marked white line; if none exists, stop before the crosswalk, or before entering the intersection when neither marking is present. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

A shared middle turning lane serves left-turning vehicles approaching from either direction and is not a through-travel or passing lane.
